newsitem.title: CHINA: China nabs man for handing out leaflets in square.
newsitem.headline: China nabs man for handing out leaflets in square.

text.p: Police have detained a Chinese man for handing out leaflets on Beijing's central Tiananmen Square demanding authorities apologise for the 1989 crackdown on a democracy campaign, a source said on Sunday.

The man, identified only by his surname Sun, was taken into custody last week when he was found distributing leaflets on the square near the Great Hall of the People, where parliament was in session, the source said.
"By the time police noticed and arrested him, he had handed out more than 100 counter-revolutionary leaflets," said the source who asked not to be identified.
Counter-revolution is communist jargon for subversion.
The leaflets demanded authorities apologise for sending in troops and tanks to crush demonstrations for democracy on June 3-4, 1989 with heavy loss of life, the source said.
Tiananmen Square was the centre of the student-led protests in 1989.

The flyers also slammed as a "sell-out" the late leader Deng Xiaoping's "one country, two systems" formula under which Hong Kong will keep its capitalist system for 50 years after it returns to Chinese rule.
Hong Kong becomes a Special Administrative Region of China at midnight on June 30 after 150 years of British rule.

Deng, who died on February 19 aged 92, ordered the military crackdown on the 1989 demonstrations and is credited with creating the "one country, two systems" formula for reunifying Hong Kong with China.
China is also trying to woo rival Taiwan to reunify under the same "one country, two systems" banner, though Taiwanese leaders say they have no interest in the formula.
Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a rebel province since the communists drove the defeated Nationalist armies into exile on the island in 1949.
